latest_nl_proof: Fix an arbitrary real number x, and let m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer, m <= x, and m is the greatest integer with this property. Suppose, for contradiction, that x >= m + 1. Then m + 1 is an integer and also m + 1 <= x. But this contradicts the maximality of m, since m + 1 > m is a larger integer that still does not exceed x. Therefore the assumption is impossible, so x < m + 1. Substituting m = floor(x), we obtain x < floor(x) + 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
role_in_parent: Provides the standard upper floor bound used upstream to prove x - floor(x) < 1.
statement_nl: For every real number x, x < floor(x) + 1.

domain_restrictions: floor(x) is interpreted as the greatest integer less than or equal to x
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all real x, with k defined as floor(x) (the greatest integer less than or equal to x), it holds that x < k + 1.
